title: Fix CLI Performance Death Spiral From Cache Invalidation
description: Fix the massive performance problem where CLI processes consume 100-200% CPU each. Root cause: hashSemioMetaState walks .repo including ⚡ (agent session logs) directory, which changes on every hook invocation, invalidating the tree cache and forcing full rebuilds on every search. This creates a death spiral of hooks → file writes → cache invalidation → expensive rebuilds.
summary: Fixed CLI performance death spiral caused by tree cache invalidation on every hook call. The hashSemioMetaState function was walking the entire .repo directory including ⚡ (agent session logs, 1772+ files) and using file modtimes for 🎫 (ticket) files. Since every hook call writes to both directories, the cache fingerprint changed on every tool use, forcing a full 8-10 second tree rebuild on every search. Fix: (1) Skip ⚡ directory entirely from hash - these are ephemeral hook artifacts irrelevant to tree structure. (2) Skip file contents/modtimes for ticket files under 🎫 - only track directory existence so cache invalidates on ticket open/close but not on every hook's agent tracking update. Result: cached search drops from ~9s to ~0.4s (20x improvement). Cache fingerprint is now stable across hook invocations.
